h1: Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok — 5-Star Rama IV with 50m Pool, Onsen & MedPark Hospital Nearby
intro: Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok is a brand-new 5-star hotel that opened in 2025 on Rama IV Road in Sathon, central Bangkok. Its 512 rooms span floors 29 to 50 with city and Lumphini Park views. For families accompanying patients at MedPark Hospital, the location is particularly practical — the hospital sits on the same Rama IV Road just roughly 1 km away, reachable in about 7 minutes by car. MRT Lumphini (Exit 1A) is a 3-minute walk, and One Bangkok luxury mall is right next door. Families are especially drawn to the hotel's 50-metre saltwater infinity pool, Japanese onsen, Tiny Tree Kids Club, and free Games Room with PS5 and arcade machines — enough to keep children entertained for an entire stay without leaving the building. Scored 9.2 out of 10 from 2,934 real guest reviews on Agoda. Rooms from approx. THB 4,500/night.

body.html: Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok opened its doors in 2025 on a prime stretch of Rama IV Road, sandwiched between One Bangkok mall and Lumphini Park — Bangkok's version of Central Park. The 50-floor tower greets guests with a lobby pond and the signature scent of paradise flowers, a deliberate nod to the park across the street. Families travelling alongside patients receiving care at MedPark Hospital will find the geography genuinely convenient: the hospital sits on the same Rama IV Road, a straight shot of about 1 km — roughly 7 minutes by car or a short Grab ride.

The 512 rooms occupy floors 29 to 50, all fitted with 55-inch Smart TVs, Nespresso machines, Dyson hairdryers, jetted bathtubs and a daily-replenished complimentary minibar. Standard Premium King Rooms at 44 sq m start from roughly THB 4,500–7,000 per night depending on season. Connecting rooms (88 sq m, sleeping up to 4 adults and 2 children) suit families perfectly. Executive Suites reach 88 sq m with a separate living area; the Family Executive Suite stretches to 132 sq m; and the Lumphini Penthouse tops out at 176 sq m.
"The 50-metre pool is stunning with full city views. The kids absolutely refused to leave the Games Room — PS5, arcade, billiards, all free. We didn't need to go anywhere the entire stay."

The entire 27th floor is devoted to leisure and wellness. The 50-metre saltwater infinity pool and Jacuzzi command panoramic Bangkok skyline views, with reviews consistently calling it one of Bangkok's finest hotel pools. The Tiny Tree Kids Club, developed in partnership with Plantoy and inspired by Montessori principles, offers wooden toys, a LEGO zone, playhouses and slides at no extra charge for guests. The free Games Room packs in PS5 consoles, racing simulators, pinball, billiards and darts — families reported children spending entire afternoons here while parents rested. The Gravity Fit Club gym covers 1,400 sq m with Italian TechnoGym equipment and hosts yoga classes. Rounding it all out is Let's Relax Onsen & Spa, offering authentic Japanese hot springs alongside steam rooms, saunas, aromatherapy and body wraps.

Dining runs across four venues. Malai Restaurant handles all-day global dining including a breakfast buffet that reviewers rate highly — freshly cooked Pad Thai, wonton soup, congee, eggs to order and a Thai milk tea soft-serve that gets a special mention. Level 50 Rooftop offers 360-degree Bangkok views from the top floor; some reviews note the rooftop kitchen can struggle to keep pace during busy service. Bloom and Brew Café handles wellness-focused coffee and light bites. One important note for guests who enjoy a drink: the entire Grande Centre Point chain operates a no-alcohol policy across all its restaurants — this is a dealbreaker for some. One Bangkok mall next door has plenty of bars and restaurants if needed.

The Rama IV Road location works well for anyone with a medical reason for being in the area. MRT Lumphini (Exit 1A) is a 3-minute walk, providing clean and affordable connections to Silom, Sukhumvit and Asok (the interchange for the Airport Rail Link to Suvarnabhumi). One Bangkok immediately adjacent covers shopping, dining and convenience. MedPark Hospital is the same road heading east toward Khlong Toei, roughly 1 km away — no complicated routing required.

Honest observations from the real guest record: soundproofing in some rooms is inconsistent — multiple reviewers noted they could hear corridor conversations and noise from adjacent rooms. A handful of early guests flagged a faint formaldehyde smell typical of a brand-new building, which tends to dissipate over time. Room service arrives slowly and is priced considerably above the Malai Restaurant menu. Elevator waits during peak hours (early morning and evening) drew comment. On the positive side, the building is genuinely pristine, the room hardware is excellent, and most guest interactions with staff are described as warm, proactive and professional.

honestSummary: Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok offers a combination of location, family amenities and 5-star finish that is hard to match at this price point among Bangkok's newest hotels. For families with a member receiving treatment at MedPark Hospital, the proximity, the free kids' facilities and the MRT connection make practical sense. As a hotel that opened in 2025, some operational rough edges remain — uneven soundproofing, slow room service and inconsistent rooftop management — but the core hardware and most of the team are genuinely impressive.
honestChecks: If you are a light sleeper — several reviewers reported hearing corridor conversations through their room doors due to inconsistent soundproofing. Request a high-floor corner room at check-in for the best chance of quiet.

If drinking alcohol at the hotel matters to you — the entire Grande Centre Point chain serves no alcohol in any of its restaurants or bars. One Bangkok mall next door has plenty of options, but it is worth knowing before you book.

If budget is a primary concern — high-season rates can reach THB 7,000–10,000/night, and room service pricing adds up quickly. Compare rates with well-reviewed 4-star hotels in the same area before committing.

tips.title: Getting to MedPark Hospital
tips.body: MedPark Hospital is roughly 1 km east along Rama IV Road. Grab takes about 7 minutes and costs very little. Alternatively, MRT Lumphini is 3 minutes' walk from the hotel; MedPark is a short ride-share from the Khlong Toei / Queen Sirikit area.

tips.title: Pool is quietest in the early morning
tips.body: The 50-metre saltwater pool gets busy from mid-morning, especially on weekends and public holidays. Head down before 9 am for the calmest swim and the best light for photos.

tips.title: Games Room is free, no booking needed
tips.body: The Games Room is complimentary for all hotel guests, walk-in anytime. It includes PS5 consoles, racing simulators, billiards, darts, pinball and arcade machines — a useful distraction for children during long waits or recovery days.

tips.title: Beat the breakfast rush
tips.body: Malai Restaurant's breakfast buffet is well-regarded but fills up quickly between 8 and 9 am. Aim to arrive before 8 am or after 9:30 am for a calmer experience and fresher food replenishments.

faqTitle: FAQ — Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok and which MRT station is closest?
faq.a: The hotel is at 1188 Rama IV Road, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok 10120. The nearest station is MRT Lumphini (Exit 1A), a 3-minute walk (0.21 km). The hotel is also directly adjacent to One Bangkok luxury mall and faces Lumphini Park.

faq.q: How far is Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok from MedPark Hospital?
faq.a: MedPark Hospital is roughly 1 km away along the same Rama IV Road, in the direction of Khlong Toei. The journey by car or Grab takes about 7 minutes. There is no need to change roads, making it highly convenient for families accompanying patients.

faq.q: What are the room types and prices at Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok?
faq.a: Rooms start from around THB 4,500/night for a Premium King Room (44 sq m). Premium Connecting rooms (88 sq m, sleeping up to 4 adults and 2 children) begin around THB 7,500. Executive Suites (88 sq m) start from roughly THB 10,000. The Family Executive Suite (132 sq m) runs around THB 14,000. Rates vary significantly by season and advance booking — compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok good for families with children?
faq.a: Yes — it is one of the most family-equipped 5-star hotels in Bangkok. The Tiny Tree Kids Club (Montessori-inspired, free for guests) and the complimentary Games Room (PS5, arcade, billiards, darts) keep children occupied for hours. The 50-metre pool has space for children, connecting and family suite rooms sleep up to 6, and breakfast covers all ages.

faq.q: What pool and spa facilities does the hotel have?
faq.a: Floor 27 houses a 50-metre saltwater infinity pool with panoramic Bangkok skyline views, plus a Jacuzzi. Let's Relax Onsen & Spa provides authentic Japanese hot springs (onsen), steam rooms, saunas, aromatherapy and body-wrap treatments. Gravity Fit Club is a 1,400 sq m gym with Italian TechnoGym equipment and yoga classes.

faq.q: Does Grande Centre Point Lumphini Bangkok serve alcohol?
faq.a: No. The entire Grande Centre Point chain operates a no-alcohol policy — no alcoholic drinks are served in any restaurant or bar on the property. Guests who wish to drink can head to the adjacent One Bangkok mall, which has a wide range of bars and restaurants.
